text:
The Dylan Larkin saga is over, and tonight is the first home game of whatever Detroit is now. Larkin asked for a trade in the summer, lost the captaincy in September, told the club on Oct. 29 he would no longer play for it and was suspended. On Sunday he was traded to Montreal for Kirby Dach, top prospect Michael Hage, goalie Sam Montembeault and four picks, including two conditional firsts, and he has already debuted for the Canadiens. Interim GM Shawn Horcoff has said it isn't a rebuild. Dach could make his Red Wings debut tonight.

The team he left is 1-4-0 in its last five with only 39% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in those games, and it hasn't won the chance battle once in that stretch. The one thing holding up is the goaltending. Daniil Tarasov is at .927 with 9.2 goals saved above expected this season, and he has stopped 3.8 more than expected over his last five starts while going 1-4-0. That's a goalie doing his job for a team that isn't scoring: Detroit has finished 12.2 goals below what its chances usually produce. Viktor Arvidsson has gone ten games without a goal on 3.0 expected.

Vancouver arrives in worse shape on paper. The Canucks take 40% of the five-on-five expected goals, allow the most expected goals per 60 in the league and take 4.2 penalties a game. They traded Max Sasson to the Rangers, and attendance at home has hit a 25-year low, the clearest sign of a rebuild that fans support in principle. Elias Pettersson is listed day-to-day with an upper-body injury but traveled to see a specialist on this trip. The bright spot is Brock Boeser, on an 11-game point streak, and Filip Hronek is one goal from 50 in his career, back in the building where he started.

Our numbers have Detroit at 3.76 expected goals to Vancouver's 2.53. Our sleepers both wear red: Michael Brandsegg-Nygård (21% to score) and Marco Kasper (39% for a point), each with a matchup that flatters them.
headline: The Red Wings' first night after Dylan Larkin
